rationale: Tests the H1 vs H2 receptor distinction — the foundational concept established in this block on allergic rhinitis pathophysiology and histamine receptor roles.

Tests a common misconception about WHY second-generation antihistamines avoid sedation — the pharmacokinetic (P-glycoprotein efflux) vs pharmacodynamic distinction established in the classification block.
Applies the PK/adverse-effect profiles just covered to a clinical prescribing scenario where sedation is a safety-critical concern.

Tests the counter-intuitive fexofenadine–fruit juice interaction via OATP inhibition — the specific clinical pearl this block establishes, which contradicts the common assumption about grapefruit juice.

Tests whether students understand that the three therapeutic goals (analgesia, anti-inflammation, antipyresis) are mechanistically separable — specifically that paracetamol lacks meaningful anti-inflammatory activity despite being an effective analgesic.
Tests understanding of the systemic (not merely local) mechanism of NSAID gastropathy — the central ADR concept established in the block on adverse drug reactions.
Applies the clinical decision-making framework from this block — balancing GI risk, cardiovascular risk, and anti-inflammatory efficacy when low-dose aspirin is co-administered.
Tests the triple whammy mechanism described in this clinical pearl — analysing how three drug classes simultaneously impair renal compensatory mechanisms to cause acute kidney injury.
Tests understanding of the molecular mechanism driving the acute gout attack — the NLRP3 inflammasome/IL-1β axis established as the central pathophysiological concept in this block.
Tests ability to sequence the gout management plan correctly — the critical dual-phase approach detailed in this block, where premature allopurinol initiation is a classic prescribing error.

Tests the critical distinction between OA (symptomatic management) and RA (requires DMARDs) — the central management principle in this block, where failing to start a DMARD in RA leads to irreversible joint destruction.

Tests the ability to identify the MOST critical prescribing concern (teratogenicity) when choosing migraine prophylaxis in a woman of childbearing age — the key safety evaluation in this block's management plan.
